name: Datum Flow
tagline: Fluid flow simulation: draw it, set the flow, see and check the results.
for: Mechanical, process, HVAC and energy engineers; researchers; students and lecturers.
about: Datum Flow simulates fluid flow on the desktop. Draw a region or pick a template, choose the fluid, say where it comes in, where it leaves and where the walls are, and Datum Flow meshes it, solves it and shows the velocity, pressure and temperature.

It gives the numbers engineers need (pressure drop, flow rate, drag and lift, heat transfer) and proves its answers: every release ships a verification report that compares the solver with exact solutions and published benchmarks.

steps.title: Draw the geometry
steps.text: Rectangles, circles, polygons and arcs, added together or cut out as bodies in the flow. Or start from a template: channel, cavity, step, cylinder, heated box.

steps.title: Set the flow
steps.text: Choose water, air, a light oil or your own fluid. Mark the inlets, outlets, walls and symmetry lines, and set temperatures if heat matters. Datum Flow checks the setup and says what is missing.

steps.title: See and check the results
steps.text: Contours, arrows and streamlines; probes and line plots; flow rate, pressure drop, forces and heat flow. Help › Verification shows how the solver compares with known answers.

highlights: The Datum window: ribbon, sidebar of views, a step-by-step Setup, printing and an updater
2D steady laminar flow, with heat and natural convection
Its own finite-element solver, written in Rust, inside the app
Automatic meshing with refinement at walls, corners and wakes, and a mesh quality report
A setup check that refuses to solve and says why: no outlet, an edge with no boundary, a flow that is probably turbulent
Contours, arrows and streamlines; probes and line plots; flow rate, pressure drop, drag and lift, heat flow and Nusselt number
Residuals and monitors plotted while it solves; stop and resume; plain advice when it does not converge
PDF report, VTU for free viewers, CSV, PNG; DXF outlines in; a command-line tool
A verification report in every release: exact solutions, order of accuracy, published benchmarks
